importance_ranking.reason: Significant visual variation across material types (PUF panel vs FRP vs GI sheet vs ACP) and size configurations — buyers use the image to identify construction type and assess build quality before reading any text. Wrong material appearance or size impression causes an immediate skip.

Built type (material) and size are non-interchangeable primary shortlisting criteria — a PUF panel cabin cannot substitute for FRP in a corrosive environment, and a 4x4 cannot substitute for an 8x6 at a site with a fixed footprint allocation. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated.

Indian facility managers and contractors compare prices aggressively, but price is only comparable after material type and size match — both dimensions drive price substantially. Listed price is a budget entry point; final price is negotiated based on exact configuration.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall — siblings are material/type-based (FRP Cabin, PUF Cabin, MS Security Cabins) and buyers search by spec and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer status, installation capability, AMC availability, and BMTPC/MHA compliance credentials are evaluated during vendor selection — particularly for government and institutional buyers — but company ranks after spec and price confirmation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Large bespoke multi-guard complexes may be quoted per project with a BOQ, but standard single-unit cabins are always per piece — no buyer ever questions this.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied by the product — a complete prefabricated structure is always sold per piece. No buyer questions whether a security cabin is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the cabin's material class (PUF Panel / FRP / GI / ACP / MS / PVC / Cement Board) — values are non-interchangeable across site requirements and carry the largest price delta in the category.
Defines the cabin footprint (4x4 through 12x10) — non-interchangeable with site allocation and directly scales price; a 4x4 cannot substitute for an 8x6.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Height is a standard cabin dimension called out in government and institutional specs (7 ft is the most common standard) and affects headroom, ventilation fitment, and AC installation — sellers need it to confirm supply and price accurately.
Flat vs sloped/pitched roof affects water drainage performance and aesthetic suitability for gated communities and institutional sites — buyers in these segments often specify roof type explicitly.
Sliding vs swing door is a functional requirement at space-constrained entry points — sellers need this to confirm the cabin configuration matches the site's access geometry.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Material class routes the RFQ to sellers who manufacture in the required construction type — a seller specialising in FRP cabins cannot supply a PUF Panel cabin, and material determines thermal performance and compliance eligibility.
Primary footprint dimension gives sellers enough context to confirm they can supply the required size and to price accurately for the buyer's site allocation.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Height is a standard structural dimension that sellers need alongside footprint to confirm supply capability and price accurately — a taller cabin requires proportionally more material and affects AC/ventilation fitment.

Buyers in hot climates or under government specs often require PUF insulation specifically — sellers need this to confirm thermal performance compliance, as a GI or MS cabin can be insulated or uninsulated.
